sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Delaware?
sections.html:
You record a deed with the Recorder of Deeds in the county where the land sits, which means New Castle, Kent or Sussex County. Title 25 of the Delaware Code says a deed recorded in one county only has effect for land in that county.

The three offices are separate, and each sets its own fee schedule. State law says the fees of the New Castle and Sussex recorders are set by ordinance, and Kent's are set the same way.

  • New Castle County: 800 N. French St., 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801. The recorder's office phone is (302) 395-7700.
  • Kent County: the Deeds Office at the county administrative complex, 555 Bay Rd., Dover. Kent lists (302) 744-2300 and weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Sussex County: 2 The Circle, Georgetown, DE 19947. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, and the recording window closes at 4:00 p.m.

New Castle's recorder describes the office as the repository for all land transaction records, corporate filings and financing statements in the county. Sussex County says its office's mission is recording and indexing documents correctly and collecting the right fees and taxes.

sections.h2: What does the recorder require before accepting a Delaware deed?
sections.html:
The recorder will not accept a deed until it meets a short list of statutory requirements. The list below comes from 9 Del. C. section 9605 and 30 Del. C. chapter 54.

  • Affidavit of residence and gain: a deed conveying title to real estate must come with the affidavit unless the transfer is one of the exempt transactions in the transfer tax law.
  • Preparer's name: the deed must contain the words "prepared by" followed by the name and address of the person who drafted it.
  • Value: the deed must state the true, full and complete value, or come with an affidavit that gives the value and the reason, if any, that the deed is not taxable.
  • Proof of tax: no taxable document is recorded without proof that the realty transfer tax was paid.
  • Correct fees: Kent County says deeds cannot be recorded until the correct fees and taxes are collected, and a $20 rejection fee may apply.

Some deeds need extra language. If a lot in an unincorporated suburban community fronts a private road that the State does not maintain, the deed must say so before the recorder can record it.

Anyone who prepares a deed for a sale to a cash buyer should treat this list as a checklist. A missing preparer line or affidavit means a rejected deed and a closing that slips.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Delaware?
sections.html:
Recording fees are small next to the transfer tax, and they vary by county. Kent County publishes a schedule effective June 1, 2024, and New Castle County has announced an increase effective September 28, 2026.

Every recorded document also carries two statutory charges. Under 9 Del. C. section 9607, the recorder collects a $5 Housing Development Fund surcharge and a $25 Delaware Cultural Access Fund fee, and these are included in the county's assessment fee.

Sussex County's fee schedule was not available in the pages we reviewed, so call (302) 855-7785 before you send a check.

sections.h2: What is the Delaware realty transfer tax and who pays it?
sections.html:
The realty transfer tax is 3 percent of the property's value, or 2.5 percent where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5 percent local tax. The statute says it is split equally between grantor and grantee, and section 5412 puts the burden on the grantor unless the parties agree otherwise.

The Delaware Code counts "value" as the actual consideration, including liens and encumbrances. If the price is lower than the highest appraised value for local tax purposes, value means that appraised figure unless a party shows fair market value is lower. The code says proof of an arm's length sale between unrelated parties is enough to show fair market value.

A few rules matter to sellers in particular:

  • No tax applies if the value is under $100.
  • A first-time home buyer's share is reduced by one half of one percent of the lesser of the value or $400,000. The reduction applies to the grantee's portion only and does not lower the seller's.
  • Payment is shown by documentary stamp or another method the Department of Finance allows, and the recorder acts as the stamp agent.
  • On a judicial sale, the tax is paid first out of the proceeds, ahead of other claims and costs.

The code sets penalties for avoiding the tax. Presenting a document without the full tax paid is unlawful, with a fine up to $500 and up to one year in prison.

Municipal rates can add to the county's. Kent County's recorder publishes a rate form for state, county and municipal taxes, and its page directs tax questions to the Division of Revenue Tax Conferee at (302) 577-8651.

sections.h2: Which Delaware deeds are exempt from realty transfer tax?
sections.html:
Section 5401 of Title 30 lists more than two dozen kinds of conveyance that are not taxed as documents. Several come up often in home sales and family transfers.

  • Wills and transfer on death deeds, and mortgages.
  • Conveyances between spouses, and between former spouses after the divorce decree for property acquired during the marriage.
  • Conveyances between parent and child, between siblings, and between grandparent and grandchild.
  • A conveyance to a lender holding a bona fide mortgage that is genuinely in default, whether through a sheriff's foreclosure sale or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Conveyances to or from the United States, Delaware, their agencies and political subdivisions, and certain nonprofits.
  • Conveyances to a land bank.

Exempt does not mean unrecorded. The deed or an accompanying affidavit still has to give the value and the reason the document is exempt. For a foreclosure purchase by the lender, the grantee makes the affidavit.

If you inherit a Delaware house and want to deed it to a sibling, the sibling exemption can apply. A tax professional or attorney should confirm the exemption before closing.

sections.h2: Can I record a Delaware deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, if the county recorder has chosen to accept electronic documents. The electronic recording subchapter of Title 25 lets a recorder receive, index and store electronic documents under standards set by the Electronic Recording Commission, which includes each county's recorder and two members appointed by the Secretary of State.

A recorder that accepts electronic documents must keep accepting paper ones and must index both in the same index. Fees and taxes may be collected electronically. An electronic signature satisfies a signature requirement, and notarization can be met when the notary's electronic signature and other required information are attached to the document.

Sussex County's recorder runs a recording activity notification service, and its deed records are searchable online, and Kent County links an online deed search from its Deeds Office page. Each office decides what it will accept, so ask before you plan on e-recording.

sections.h2: Does a nonresident seller owe tax at recording?
sections.html:
A nonresident seller may have estimated income tax collected at the recorder's counter. Under 9 Del. C. section 9607(e), before the recorder records a deed from a nonresident individual, pass-through entity or corporation, the recorder collects the required tax return and the estimated income tax reported due, if any.

The recorder remits that money to the Secretary of Finance by the 20th of the month after recording. This applies to the seller's state income tax on a gain, and it is separate from the transfer tax.

Owners who live outside Delaware, which is common for inherited and rental property, should ask the closing agent about this return early. A missing return holds up the deed.

faqs.q: How long does it take to record a deed in Delaware?
faqs.a: The pages reviewed do not state a standard turnaround. Sussex County closes its recording window at 4:00 p.m. each business day, and the recorder notes the date of reception once the instrument is received. Ask the office or your title company for current timing.

faqs.q: What is the Delaware realty transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The state statute sets 3 percent of value, or 2.5 percent where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5 percent local tax. The tax is shared equally by buyer and seller unless the contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax in Delaware, the buyer or the seller?
faqs.a: The statute apportions it equally between grantor and grantee. As between the parties, the grantor bears the burden unless they agree differently, so the sales contract controls.

faqs.q: Is there a first-time home buyer break on Delaware transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer's share is reduced by one half of one percent of the lesser of the value or $400,000. The break applies to the buyer's portion only.

faqs.q: What does the recorder need on the deed?
faqs.a: A deed needs a stated value or value affidavit, proof of transfer tax payment unless exempt, an affidavit of residence and gain, and the words "prepared by" with the preparer's name and address.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed without paying the fees up front?
faqs.a: No. The recorder may require payment once the date of reception is noted, and Kent County says deeds cannot be recorded until the correct fees and taxes are collected.
